extracted.intended_audience: TeX users / typists / macro writers learning TeX internals and typesetting
extracted.subtask_short: typesetting with TeX boxes and glue
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for constructing and manipulating TeX boxes (hbox, vbox), and for specifying and reasoning about glue (natural space, stretch, shrink, and infinite orders), including sentence-spacing rules and interline spacing behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box model: characters, lines, pages are boxes
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX represents the letter 'A' as a character box, a line of type as an hbox, and a page as a vbox built from a vertical list of line-boxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you need ordinary text you don't have to think about boxes; use explicit \hbox and \vbox only when you want complete control over where each letter/line goes (examples: \vbox{\hbox{Two lines}\hbox{of type.}}). Boxes can be nested to arbitrary depth for complex formulas/tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \hbox and \vbox for explicit control
rubrics_metrics.description: If you want to 'retain complete control over where each letter goes' you must use \hbox and \vbox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \setbox0=\hbox{T\kern-.1667em\lower.5ex\hbox{E}\kern-.12Sem X} constructs a boxed logo. Otherwise let TeX choose line divisions automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character boxes include height and depth information
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX font characters have variable height and depth information (not all characters share same metrics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variable heights/depths allow TeX to align by baselines and to position accents and mathematical symbols correctly; font designers supply these metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Glue has three attributes: natural space, stretch, shrink
rubrics_metrics.description: Glue is specified as {dimen} plus {dimen} minus {dimen}; the three attributes are the natural space, its ability to stretch, and its ability to shrink.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example glue specification: natural=9, stretch=3, shrink=1. The natural width of a list includes the natural widths of glue components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Glue setting: compute stretch/shrink proportionally by available units
rubrics_metrics.description: When a box must be widened (or narrowed), TeX computes how much glue must stretch (or shrink) and distributes that change among glue globs proportionally to their declared stretchability (or shrinkability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustration: to expand total box by 6 units when total stretchability is 9, multiply each unit of stretchability by 6/9 and add that amount to each glue's natural width.

rubrics_metrics.name: Glue never shrinks beyond stated shrinkability; stretching can be arbitrarily large if positive
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX will not shrink glue more than its specified shrink component; but glue with positive stretch component may stretch arbitrarily far (subject to glue-order rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a glue with shrink 1 will never become narrower than natural-1; TeX will not shrink a list to less than the sum of natural widths minus total shrinkability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing glue components: natural, stretch, shrink guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Natural glue space should be the amount that looks best; (b) glue stretch should be the maximum space that can be added before layout looks bad; (c) glue shrink should be the maximum amount removable before layout looks bad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designers usually specify glue types globally (formats/macros) rather than sprinkling explicit dimensions; use semantic macros like \smallskip to express intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer semantic skip macros (\smallskip, \medskip, \bigskip)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of putting explicit point dimensions throughout a manuscript, use named skips so you can change definitions later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain TeX defines \smallskip (3pt plus 1pt minus 1pt), \medskip (two smallskips), and \bigskip (two medskips). Use these macros rather than hard-coded dims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Syntax for glue: \vskip/\hskip {dimen} plus{dimen} minus{dimen}
rubrics_metrics.description: Vertical glue: \vskip(glue); Horizontal glue: \hskip(glue). The plus and minus parts are optional and default to zero if absent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \enskip is \hskip.5em\relax (no stretch or shrink). Add \relax after a dimension when needed to prevent parsing 'plus'/'minus' as a keyword.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infinite glue orders (fil, fill, filll) and primitives for them
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX recognizes multiple orders of infinity for glue: fil (first order), fill (second), and filll (third). Primitives like \vfil, \vfill, \hfil, \hfill, \hss, and their 'neg' variants manipulate these infinities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \hfil at both ends to center; \hfil at right to flush-right; \vfill to fill remaining vertical space. Prefer fil where possible; fill or filll only when stronger infinity needed. \hss and \vss provide infinite shrink/stretch; \hfilneg/\vfilneg cancel stretchability of \hfil/\vfil.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interword spacing: plain TeX adds extra space after sentence-ending punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Plain TeX inserts extra space at the end of a sentence and increases stretchability (and decreases shrinkability) after punctuation marks so sentence-end spaces can be larger when lines are stretched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: glue after comma stretches at 1.25× rate of ordinary interword glue; after period/exclamation/question it stretches at 3×. Shrink factors: after comma shrink is 80% of ordinary; after period/exclaim/question shrink is one third.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ~ (tie) or control-space (\ ) to prevent TeX from treating a period as sentence end
rubrics_metrics.description: When a period follows an abbreviation and should not be treated as sentence-ending, insert a tie (~) or an explicit control space (\) so TeX won't modify interword glue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer ~ after common abbreviations within names: 'Mr.~Drofnats'. Use 'Mr.\ Drofnats' when normal space but allowing a possible line break is acceptable (the line might end at the period). For bibliographic sequences use control spaces: 'Proc.\ Amer.\ Math.\ Soc.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Frenchspacing: disable sentence-end extra spacing with \frenchspacing/\nonfrenchspacing
rubrics_metrics.description: \frenchspacing makes all spaces identical regardless of punctuation; \nonfrenchspacing restores TeX's sophisticated spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \frenchspacing for bibliographies or when you don't want extra sentence spacing; you can make it local to groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Space factor mechanism controls modified interword glue
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX maintains an integer 'space factor' f (normally 1000) during horizontal list processing; it modifies the normal interword glue by: adding extra space if f>=2000, multiplying stretch component by f/1000, and multiplying shrink by 1000/f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Space factor starts at 1000 at beginning of list, is set to character space factor codes when characters appear, set to 1000 after non-character boxes or math formulas. Use \spacefactor=(number) to assign explicitly if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overriding font spacing with \spaceskip and \xspaceskip
rubrics_metrics.description: If \xspaceskip is nonzero and f>=2000, \xspaceskip glue is used for interword space; else if \spaceskip is nonzero it is used (with stretch/shrink modified by space factor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Macros like \raggedright use \spaceskip and \xspaceskip to suppress all stretching and shrinking of interword spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Space factor codes per character (\sfcode) affect sentence detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Each character has a space factor code; INITEX defaults codes to 1000 except some uppercase letters; plain TeX redefines some (e.g., \sfcode'.'=3000) so punctuation acts appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TeX doesn't consider period/question/exclaim as sentence end if preceding character is uppercase (interpreted as initials). Use \sfcode to tweak behavior; \frenchspacing resets \sfcode of '.' to 1000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ligatures and special characters affect space factor computation
rubrics_metrics.description: When ligatures are formed or when a character specified via \char is used, TeX computes the space factor code from the characters that generated the ligature; some ligatures (e.g., the double-right-quote) are given special handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain TeX sets the space factor code for single-right-quote to zero so punctuation effects propagate; double-quote ligature's sfcode is never examined by TeX in plain TeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kerns are fixed (non-flexible) spacing and differ from glue
rubrics_metrics.description: A \kern inserts fixed space that cannot stretch or shrink; TeX never breaks a line at a kern unless it is immediately followed by glue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kerns are used for small adjustments (e.g., in logos). Use glue if you want flexible spacing that can be adjusted during line setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative dimensions and backspaces are allowed for widths (but heights/depths nonnegative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Boxes may have negative width (e.g., fonts can declare negative character widths acting as backspace); heights and depths of constructed hboxes are never negative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negative box widths are used occasionally (e.g., for right-to-left handling), but TeX's line-breaking assumes words don't have negative widths so this is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspect box contents with \showbox for diagnostics
rubrics_metrics.description: Plain TeX will display the contents of a box register (e.g., \showbox0) in the log file, showing nested \hbox entries, kerns, glue amounts, shifts, and font items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \showbox to debug exactly what TeX thinks it's doing (e.g., inspect interword glue values, ligatures, kerns, and shifts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Glue 'orders' and glue-set algorithm for hbox/vbox construction
rubrics_metrics.description: When TeX sets glue for a box it computes totals of stretch/shrink per infinity-order (fil, fill, filll). If x < desired width, it picks the highest order with nonzero total stretch J_j and computes glue set ratio r = (desired - natural)/J_j; analogous for shrinking, with r normally (natural - desired)/z_j but limited so maximum shrink not exceeded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only glue of the highest noncanceled glue-order is modified; other glue keeps its natural width. This ensures infinities dominate and that cancellation between orders is respected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating fixed-width or spread boxes: \hbox to and \hbox spread
rubrics_metrics.description: \hbox to{dimen}{contents} creates an hbox of exact width dimen; \hbox spread{dimen}{contents} creates a box whose width is natural_width + dimen; plain \hbox{contents} uses natural width.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The \line macro is an abbreviation for \hbox to\hsize; use \hbox spread when you want to add a precise amount of stretching/shrinking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline, height, depth semantics of constructed hbox
rubrics_metrics.description: The baseline of a constructed hbox is the common baseline of interior boxes; height/depth are the maxima by which interior boxes extend above/below baseline; constructed hbox never has negative height or depth but width may be negative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When composing boxes (e.g., with \lower or \raise), the positions of internal reference points affect the outer box's baseline/height/depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interline spacing primitives: \baselineskip, \lineskip, \lineskiplimit
rubrics_metrics.description: To stack boxes vertically with consistent baseline spacing, a format designer sets \baselineskip (glue), \lineskip (glue), and \lineskiplimit (dimen). TeX attempts to make baseline distance equal to \baselineskip, but if that would bring top of new box closer than \lineskiplimit to bottom of previous box, \lineskip is used instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents lines from being too close when tall or deep letters are present; use these parameters to tune interline spacing in formats.
